site.name: Uchkun
site.tagline: How did we get here? The story of science, one step at a time.

home.question: How did we get here?
home.lead: From Thales to CRISPR: every discovery stood on an earlier one. Fall into time and watch how slowly it started, and how fast it got.

about.title: About Uchkun
about.lead: Uchkun is Kyrgyz for spark. This site tells how humanity got from Thales to artificial intelligence, one step at a time, in four languages, for curious people who are not scientists.
about.quote: If I went back to those centuries with what I know now, I could do nothing. I could not find electricity, or medicine, or build a single machine. We use everything as though we knew it, but we know almost none of it.
about.why: That sentence is the spirit of the project. This is not an encyclopaedia; it is a journey through wonder. Every event asks how one discovery stood on an earlier one, and what the people of that day did not yet know.
about.who: One person builds it, in the evenings, and he is not a historian or a scientist. All four languages are equal citizens here: Kyrgyz is not an afterthought.

form.yearHint: Integer. Negative = BCE (e.g. -585). There is no year 0.
form.placePrecision: How well the place is known

form.placeNameHint: Bare name, no "around": Samarkand, Central Asia.
form.coordsHint: Decimal degrees. North and east are positive.
form.title: Title
form.summaryHint: One or two sentences; shown on the timeline card.
form.bodyHint: Markdown: headings, lists, tables, pictures, video, formulas. 300–600 words.
form.whyItMattersHint: 2–3 sentences, highlighted box on the detail page.
form.ifYouWereThereHint: 1–2 sentences: what people did not know that day.
form.disciplinesHint: At least one. The first checked one is primary.
form.slugHint: Left empty: derived from the title.
form.statusHint: Only published events appear on the site.
form.uncredited: No credit on: {names}. Write "Author · Licence · https://source" in quotes after the link.
form.sourceLocaleHint: The language this event was written in; the others fall back to it.
form.sourcesHint: At least two independent ones, and one of them an encyclopedia.
form.peopleHint: Shared across events: a name saved here is that person's name everywhere. Years and role may stay empty.
form.buildsOnHint: Earlier events this one rests on. Only this direction is stored; the other appears by itself.
form.linkNote: In one line, what it took from it
form.imagePathHint: A path in the images bucket, or a full https address. Leave empty for no picture.

help.title: How to write Markdown
help.intro: The body of an event is written in Markdown: plain text plus a few marks. Everything below works in the Write box, and the Preview tab shows the result before you save.

rows.headings: A line beginning with ### is a section heading.
rows.emphasis: One star around a word leans it, two make it heavy.
rows.list: A line starting with a dash is a bullet; starting with a number, a numbered list.
rows.link: The words in brackets are shown, the address in parentheses is where they go.
rows.image: After the address, in quotes: author, licence and the page the picture came from. Attribution is not optional.
rows.video: A YouTube address alone on its own line turns into a player.
rows.callout: A box that stands out. NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION and THEORY each get their own colour.
rows.code: Three backticks above and below keep the text as typed, in a fixed-width font.
rows.formula: Between single dollars a formula sits in the line; between double dollars it gets a line of its own.
rows.table: Columns separated by pipes; the second row of dashes is what makes it a table.
rows.quote: A line beginning with a greater-than sign is a quotation.
rows.rule: Three dashes on a line of their own draw a divider.
